_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. A mutation vocabulary belongs to ONE subset of ONE standard of ONE artifact, so the oracle registration and the catalog live here rather than in a shared manifest. `en1995-1-any` is generated from each triad leaf's own `SemanticDescriptor.kind`, in `#[derive(dsl::Mutations)]`'s declaration order, and `kinds_match_the_enum_and_the_catalog` in `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/🦀️.rs` fails the moment this list and the enum part company.

oracles.rationale:
🐍️ No third-party library in any ecosystem reads or writes `s.norm.en1995` — checked against PyPI, which serves no `en1995`, `eurocode`, `vdi3805` or `iso16757` distribution, and whose nearest real packages (`structuralcodes`, `concreteproperties`, `anastruct`) implement design-code formulae and speak no interchange format — so this subset's reference is a SECOND IMPLEMENTATION rather than a third-party distribution. That is why `package` is empty: the entry links no external library and contributes nothing to the dependency ratchet. The implementation is `../../../../../🧪️tests/mutate-en1995-1/🐍️.py`, all 66 kinds of `En1995Mutation` written in Python from `26/08/12/SEMANTIC-MUTATIONS-OVERHAUL`'s `📓️taxonomy.md` (verb table, the `new_<field>` naming mechanic, the addressing convention) and `📓️derivation-rules.md` (shape rules), plus this manifest's own catalog for the closed list of kinds. It imports nothing from the Rust it judges and transliterates none of it — the field a `new*` argument names is resolved by normalised spelling against the document's own keys, exactly as the naming mechanic states. Its reading is pinned by reaching every committed handcrafted `(before, mutation, after, outcome)` vector and by re-emitting the committed `.dsl.semio` artifact byte for byte, neither of which a misreading could do.

UNDER PROTOCOL V2 this registration is classified `cross-semio-implementation` — a required SUPPLEMENTAL oracle that does not discharge `en1995-1-mutate`'s external-oracle requirement for its 66-kind mutation vocabulary; a qualifying third-party reference (`third-party-library` / `third-party-cli` / `standards-reference-tool`) is still owed.

[2026-09-02, D1 — SEPARATE-ARTIFACT-STANDARD-SUBSET-IMPLEMENTATIONS-AND-FIXTURE-TEST-EVERY-MUTATION] Promoted from cross-semio-implementation to verified-native-second-implementation: this artifact is semio-native (isSemioNativeArtifact), this reference's own third-party survey above (kept verbatim) already names what was checked and declined, its python implementation differs from the Rust subject, and it covers 100% of this manifest's 1 capability/capabilities with 68 committed fixture vector(s). See .🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️09/☀️02/SEPARATE-ARTIFACT-STANDARD-SUBSET-IMPLEMENTATIONS-AND-FIXTURE-TEST-EVERY-MUTATION/📓️d1-native-oracle-discharge.md.

oracles.rationale: 🐍️ Independent-formulation compliance oracle of EN1995: the python compliance script recomputes the Rust check chain and the shared harness (`✏️s/🔌️plugins/📕️norm/🔮️oracles/🏃️harness`) replays blessed oracle cases against the third-party references claimed in the norm root registry (`norm-eurocode-structuralcodes`, `-concreteproperties`, `-sectionproperties`, `-blue-prints`, `-sympy`, `-groundhog`, scipy numerics). Labelled honestly as independent formulation, not third-party validation, wherever no library covers the clause. The document-level script `🔮️oracles/🚦️check-outcome/🐍️.py` wraps the compliance oracle and adds the design-case families (T-14, T-18, T-30 to T-33, T-45, T-46); its `--self-check` compares rectangle constants with sectionproperties, k_c with a scipy root and the beam deflection with PyNite (check-outcome case).

Reference values of the EN1995 oracle case files (`🧪️tests/🧫️fixtures/🔮️oracle-cases/third-party*.json`) for the checks mechanics.beam-continuous, mechanics.beam-span-envelope are computed by anastruct 1.7.0. The harness adapter `✏️s/🔌️plugins/📕️norm/🔮️oracles/🏃️harness/🔌️adapters/anastruct/🐍️.py` is the only importer; values are blessed from the library, never from the Rust. National Annex parameters are inputs of the cases.

Reference values of the EN1995 oracle case files (`🧪️tests/🧫️fixtures/🔮️oracle-cases/third-party*.json`) for the checks en1995.338.strength-class, en1995.7.5.natural-frequency are computed by blue-prints 0.8.0. The harness adapter `✏️s/🔌️plugins/📕️norm/🔮️oracles/🏃️harness/🔌️adapters/blueprints/🐍️.py` is the only importer; values are blessed from the library, never from the Rust. National Annex parameters are inputs of the cases.

Reference values of the EN1995 oracle case files (`🧪️tests/🧫️fixtures/🔮️oracle-cases/third-party*.json`) for the checks mechanics.beam-continuous, mechanics.beam-span-envelope are computed by PyNiteFEA 3.0.0. The harness adapter `✏️s/🔌️plugins/📕️norm/🔮️oracles/🏃️harness/🔌️adapters/pynite/🐍️.py` is the only importer; values are blessed from the library, never from the Rust. The third-party module `🔮️oracles/📐️third-party/🐍️.py` (run by the schema test `sectionproperties_and_pynite_agree_with_the_gamma_method_the_residual_section_and_the_dynamics` with `python -I`, `--check` asserts the closed-form bounds) also computes with PyNiteFEA 3.0.0 (inverse iteration on static solves, since `modal` is known wrong) the first natural frequency and mode of the T-63 strip, the T-120 girder and an orthotropic floor grillage, and the static deflection of the effective-stiffness beam of T-90 and of the tapered and curved members. National Annex parameters are inputs of the cases.

Reference values of the EN1995 third-party module `🔮️oracles/📐️third-party/🐍️.py` (run by the schema test `sectionproperties_and_pynite_agree_with_the_gamma_method_the_residual_section_and_the_dynamics` with `python -I`, `--check` asserts the closed-form bounds) are computed by sectionproperties 3.10.2: the part constants E_iA_i and E_iI_i and the rigid composite of the mechanically jointed beam T-90, the exact residual section of the reduced cross-section method T-106 (A_r, I, W_el of the notional char depth d_char,n), and the section properties of the tapered, curved and cut-out members (second moment of area of the trapezoid at x, net section with a hole or notch). Values are produced by the library, never by the Rust. National Annex parameters are inputs of the cases.

Reference values of the EN1995 third-party module `🔮️oracles/📐️third-party/🐍️.py` (run by the schema test `sectionproperties_and_pynite_agree_with_the_gamma_method_the_residual_section_and_the_dynamics` with `python -I`, `--check` asserts the closed-form bounds) computed by scipy 1.18.0: the creep deflection time curve u_fin(t) = u_inst (1 + k_def (1 - exp(-t/tau))) by ODE integration (solve_ivp) and the end value by quadrature, the damped floor response of EN 1995-1-1 7.3 by root finding of the resonance factor, and the quadrature of the variable-depth bending stiffness of tapered members. Values are produced by the library, never by the Rust. All k_def and damping values are inputs of the cases; the unverified registry values are not oracle truth.
